### **Job Description and Duties**

Do you want to support the ecological and economic well-being of one of the largest estuaries on the West Coast? The Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta Conservancy (Conservancy) is seeking an Environmental Scientist to develop and manage projects and grants for the Conservancy's Ecosystem Restoration and Climate Adaptation Program. This position provides an exciting opportunity to advance projects related to nature-based solutions, climate resiliency, ecosystem restoration, and agricultural sustainability in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta (Delta) and Suisun Marsh. The Conservancy is a small, committed team that works across departments and disciplines to protect, enhance, and restore the Delta's economy, agriculture and working landscapes, and environment.
  
  
In this position you will:

* Manage, monitor, and close-out projects by monitoring performance and status by tracking deliverables, budgets, and expenditures.
* Prepare and review agreements, reports, memos, documents, and invoices for the Ecosystem Restoration and Climate Adaptation Program.
* Participate in community outreach and educate interested parties about the Conservancy, its programs, and issues of importance in the Delta and Suisun Marsh
* Communicate with diverse collection of interested parties (e.g., environmental non-profits, regional conversation districts, public agencies) by preparing and presenting scientific reports, factsheets, workshops, and trainings.
* Identify, research, and address issues related to nature-based solutions, climate resiliency, ecosystem restoration, and agricultural sustainability and apply for funding for projects to implement them.
Aid Conservancy staff and management with program implementation and special projects related to environmental concerns in the Delta and Suisun Marsh.  

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program. Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program: http://hrmanual.calhr.ca.gov/Home/ManualItem/1/2113.
  
  
This position is eligible to telework up to one (1) day a week, in accordance with the Statewide Telework Policy, and will be required to report to the office as needed/required. This is subject to change based on operational need and/or future return to office orders. The successful candidate must reside in California upon appointment.
  
  
This position is designated under the Conflict of Interest Code. The position is responsible for making or participating in the making of governmental decisions that may potentially have a material effect on personal financial interests. The appointee is required to complete Form 700 within 30 days of appointment and once per year.
  
  
**This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship by the start date of employment. The Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta Conservancy does not participate in E-Verify for employment authorization purposes.**  
  
To be considered for this Environmental Scientist job opportunity, applicants must be either reachable on an employment list, have transfer eligibility or have reinstatement eligibility. To take the exam and gain employment list eligibility, please click here to access the exam bulletin:

https://calcareers.ca.gov/CalHRPublic/Search/ExamSearchResults.aspx#kw=environmental%20scientist

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

This position is located at: 1450 Halyard Drive, Suite 6, West Sacramento, CA 95691.
  
  
The incumbent works primarily indoors in an air-conditioned office building with natural and artificial lighting. The workstation is in a cubicle near others and is equipped with standard or ergonomic office equipment, as appropriate. The position requires prolonged sitting or standing and frequent use of a computer, keyboard, telephone, multifunction printer, and software applications, including but not limited to Microsoft Office Suite, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, and Adobe Acrobat.
  
  
The incumbent must collaborate with staff, other state agencies, stakeholders, and grantees to complete assigned duties and attend or coordinate meetings as needed. The position also requires the ability and willingness to perform off-site work, including site visits, tours, and events that may involve walking over uneven terrain and working outdoors in inclement weather.
  
  
Travel within California is required up to 10 percent of the time and may involve driving or riding in a state-owned vehicle, rental car, or other private or public transportation, including airplanes. Travel may occasionally require extended work hours and overnight stays.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**Senior Environmental Scientist**

**Perth, WA | Permanent, Full-time / Part-time**

RPS, a Tetra Tech company, is a leading global professional services consultancy delivering solutions across the environment, infrastructure, energy and urban development sectors.

In Australia Asia Pacific, we work with industry, government and communities to define, design and manage complex projects that create shared value. Our people combine technical expertise with practical thinking to help clients understand environmental risks, navigate complex challenges and deliver successful project outcomes.

As part of Tetra Tech, we are connected to a global network of approximately 30,000 employees, providing access to specialist expertise, opportunities and projects across Australia and internationally.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking a Senior Scientist to join our Oceans & Environment team in Perth, or Margaret River. RPS understand the importance of flexible working arrangements and this role is open to both full-time and part-time hours.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early to mid career environmental scientist who has experience in environmental approvals and is looking to continue developing their technical and consulting capability. Working alongside experienced environmental professionals, you will contribute to a range of projects.

**What you'll be involved in**

Your responsibilities will include:

* Preparing environmental approval documentation under the EP Act and EPBC Act.
* Preparing practical environmental management plans and strategies.
* Prepare and provide environmental advice to clients.
* Manage multiple tasks on a range of projects and effectively deal with conflicting priorities and work to tight deadlines.
* Prepare and provide environmental advice to clients.
* Work as part of a multi-disciplinary team and work co-operatively with people at all levels to achieve outcomes.
* Communicate and maintain good relationships with internal stakeholders, clients, suppliers and project stakeholders.

**About you**

We are looking for someone who is technically curious, practical and keen to build a career in environmental approvals and environmental consulting.

**You will ideally bring:**

* A relevant tertiary qualification in environmental management or environmental science.
* Experience in undertaking environmental impact assessments in Western Australia.
* Understanding of State and Commonwealth environmental legislation, policy and guidance.
* Good technical report writing skills and attention to detail
* Minimum of five years relevant work experience.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* The ability to work independently while knowing when to seek technical guidance
* An understanding of project delivery including quality, safety, time and budget considerations
* A commitment to ongoing professional and technical development

**Why RPS?**

Joining RPS means becoming part of a collaborative environmental team while also having access to the technical capability and opportunities of the broader Tetra Tech network.

You will have the opportunity to develop your career alongside experienced contaminated land specialists, gain exposure to a diverse range of projects and progressively take on greater technical, project and client responsibilities.

**We also offer:**

* Flexible and hybrid working arrangements where appropriate
* Professional development and career progression opportunities
* Paid professional memberships
* Active lifestyle and wellbeing initiatives
* Employee assistance and wellbeing support
* Opportunities to work with technical specialists across Australia and the wider Tetra Tech network
* A supportive and collaborative team environment
* Paid parental leave and other employee benefits

**Our commitment**

RPS is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people are respected, supported and encouraged to bring their individual perspectives and experience to work.

If you have a foundation in environmental science or contaminated land and are looking for an opportunity to deepen your technical expertise while working alongside experienced specialists, we'd like to hear from you.

**Our Approach**

Our people live our purpose, deliver our promise, and demonstrate our behaviours every day. Our behaviours define who we are. Developed by our people, they underpin everything that we do. They create the memorable experiences we are known for and make RPS a great place to do great work.  
Stronger together is one of our five core behaviours and it is key to building a collaborative workplace. We encourage everyone to bring their best and to support others to do the same. By sharing knowledge, challenging each other to think differently, and fostering an environment of trust and respect, our people can learn, grow and thrive – and share in our success.

**Recruitment Agencies**

We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on this list. Please refer to the careers page on our website if you require any further information.

jobs.description:
Overview

If you are looking for a home for the best years of your career, where you can contribute to a dynamic and innovative firm, tackle challenging project work, and collaborate with industry-recognized professionals, Geosyntec is the place for you!

We have an exciting opportunity for a Senior / Principal Sediment Remediation Engineer or Scientist
to join our Sediment Remediation and Waterfront Redevelopment practice in our Pacific Northwest Branch with offices in Portland, OR, and Boise, ID, or other Geosyntec Branches. This role will involve managing people and projects, ensuring technical excellence, and providing expertise on sediment remediation. It is ideal for a talented and highly experienced individual who is interested in being a leader and contributing to innovative and challenging projects, including the financial and technical evaluation, design, permitting, and construction stages. Our client base includes a diverse mix of industrial, institutional, and governmental clients.

Geosyntec is an innovative, international engineering and consulting firm serving private and public-sector clients to address new ventures and complex problems involving our environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. Our engineers, scientists, technical and project employees serve our clients from offices across the world. Ranked by ENR as one of the top environmental engineering design firms, Geosyntec is internationally known for its technical leadership, broad experience, and exceptional client service.

We invest in our people. Each employee is unique, and your career at Geosyntec will be too. We offer competitive pay and benefits, and well-being programs to support you and your family.

To Learn More Visit: http://www.geosyntec.com/careers/ .

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Collaboration and mentoring are cornerstones of Geosyntec’s culture. We operate under a sell-manage-do culture, and so we expect that you’d work on challenging technical projects while leveraging your existing knowledge and experience to help Geosyntec expand its current practices and capabilities through business development and client management. You may also be asked to take on project management responsibilities, along with staff management and development, and mentoring tasks. Some of the key responsibilities may include:

Managing challenging technical projects while leveraging your existing knowledge and experience to help Geosyntec expand its current practices and capabilities through business development and client management;
Task and project management, including planning and implementing investigation and remediation projects, budgeting and budget management, adherence to schedule, quality, client satisfaction, and profitability;
Evaluate contaminated sites and develop remediation approaches, including feasibility studies, removal action work plans, remediation design plans;
Lead the development of work plans, data evaluation, and cost-benefit analyses;
Implement remedial pilot tests and systems, including vendor selection, logistical coordination, permitting, and supervision of field teams;
Write technical reports, letters, memoranda, plans, specifications, and proposals; oversee and review documents prepared by project teams;
Build a portfolio of clients by winning new clients and obtaining repeat business from existing clients, leading proposal preparation, and executing a personal business development plan;
Foster trust-based relationships with clients, regulatory personnel, and other project stakeholders;
Mentor, guide, and motivate early career staff assigned in the areas of project performance, cost, schedule management, client expectations and career development; work with employees to correct deficiencies;
At times, this position may also include fieldwork including site visits, multi-media environmental sampling and characterization, drilling oversight, contractor oversight, and remediation system operations, maintenance, and construction.
Drive personal, company, and rental vehicles to client or company project or office sites, and other business locations, as needed.

Education and Licensure

Bachelor's degree in engineering (civil, chemical, or environmental preferred) or geology. (required)
Advanced degree the same. (preferred)
Professional registration (i.e., P.E. P.G.) (preferred)

Skills, Experience And Qualifications

At least 8 years (10+ years preferred) of direct environmental consulting experience in the Pacific Northwest marketplace ; or equivalent combination of education and experience. (required)
Detailed understanding of CERCLA and other applicable state regulations. (required)
Experience with multi-disciplinary project teams. (required)
Demonstrated success in the development and management of clients, and leadership skills. (required)
Ability to succeed in a fast-paced consulting environment, handling multiple project assignments, meeting strict deadlines, and traveling to client facilities as needed. (required)
Excellent writing and communication skills. (required)
Field work and overnight travel may be required.
Current OSHA 40-hr HAZWOPER training and refreshers. (preferred)
Health & Safety training, medical monitoring, and client-driven drug and background testing may be required.
Valid U.S. driver’s license and a satisfactory driving record for business travel. (required)

Job Description

The importance of water to the health of our world can’t be overstated.

As the frequency and intensity of floods, droughts and storms increases, the water industry must continue to build resiliency and lead from the front.

Together with our clients, we are thinking and doing things differently to help pre-empt and prepare for what's next. Be a part of this dynamic and committed team of diverse water specialists and drive change for your community.

You’ll be able to apply our powerful global network of skills and decades of experience to create positive water outcomes that respect nature and nurture communities.

Who are we looking for?

Whether your expertise lies in flood modelling, hydrology, hydraulic engineering, surface water, catchments, mine water management or water balance modelling, we'd love to hear from you.

We're particularly interested in professionals with strong experience in TUFLOW and/or GoldSim, who are looking to contribute to major infrastructure, mining, water infrastructure, defence, urban development, dams, tailings, environmental and digital disciplines.

Delivering flood studies, floodplain risk management studies, flood impact assessments and development impact assessments.
Conducting hydrologic and hydraulic assessments in accordance with Australian Rainfall and Runoff (ARR) methodologies.
Supporting mine water management studies, operational water assessments and strategic water planning projects.
Analysing complex catchments, water systems and flood behaviours to support informed decision making.
Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams across water resources, civil engineering, environmental services, mining, dams, tailings and planning.
Managing projects, maintaining strong client relationships and engaging with key stakeholders to deliver successful outcomes.
Contributing to proposals, business development activities and the continued growth of our water resources capability.
Conducting technical reviews and mentoring emerging professionals across the team.

Degree qualifications in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Water Resources Engineering or a related discipline.

Experience in one or more of the following areas:
Flood modelling
Hydrology
Hydraulic engineering
Surface water engineering
Mine water management
Water balance modelling
Water resources planning and assessment

Strong technical capability in one or more of the following:
TUFLOW
GoldSim

Strong communication, stakeholder engagement and client relationship skills.
Project management experience and a commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes.
A collaborative mindset and a passion for mentoring and knowledge sharing.

jobs.description:
**Practice Leader – Soils, Geochemistry, Toxicology & Risk**

  

**About SLR & the role**

What if your next leadership role could combine **world-class science, exceptional people, and genuine regional influence?** As Practice Leader for **Soils, Geochemistry, Toxicology & Risk** , you'll lead and inspire experts across Asia Pacific.

  

This team now includes our **existing Toxicology & Risk, Geochemistry and the Soils & Erosion Practices with the recent addition of our Geomorphology Practice** . With the **recent acquisition of Hydrobiology** also adding further strengths across this group. This has seen the **Practice now reach 40+ consultants** which you will be tasked with managing and growing this team further across Asia Pacific. As a newly formed grouping of some of the best in the business this provides a unique and exciting opportunity for the right person to **scale up and shape the business, delivering into this high demand sector.**

  

From mentoring future leaders to steering some of the region's most challenging environmental projects, you'll have the platform, resources and reach to make a **significant impact, while accelerating your own career in a highly visible and strategic position.**

  

SLR Consulting is an international environmental consultancy with a globally recognised reputation for providing high-quality tailored services. With offices throughout the Asia Pacific, Europe, North, Central and South America and Africa regions, we are one of a very small number of leading international specialist environmental consultants.

  

With **24 offices** in the Asia Pacific region and **1200 + staff** , SLR is on an **exciting growth trajectory** . We are flexible on location for the right person to deliver in this key role across the offices where our teams are already established and delivering exceptional work.

  

**Responsibilities**

Reporting to the **Business Unit Director – Earth Sciences,** The Practice Leader is responsible for leading people, achieving financial KPIs, growing client relationships and market share, driving technical excellence, and achieving business growth within their Practice Area, and across the wider business. Other responsibilities will include:

  

* Leading the Practice Area with authenticity, purpose and vigour
* Driving growth in line with market trends and opportunities, and actively manages resourcing requirements to facilitate growth
* Consistently achieving KPIs across the spectrum of financial metrics, responding to stretch targets as necessary
* Managing SLR’s commercial risk through rigorous and informed review of project work and proposals, ensuring adequate backlog and maintaining standards of excellence
* Using your proven leadership skills to maintain and grow a high performing practice
* Leading by example by working effectively across the Company, fostering collaboration across practices, promoting knowledge sharing regionally and globally
* Ensuring the portfolio of projects with the Practice Area is healthy, with a net positive position, and that high risks are appropriately managed
* Maintaining a client focus always. Engaging frequently with clients in collaboration with other business leaders to drive brand awareness, business development, and market share advancement both regionally and globally.
* Keeping up to date with specialist area trends and best practice, participating in technical and/or professional associations
Living and breathing the SLR way through the promotion and use of consistent globally aligned systems, practices and processes  

  

**Experience**

Our ideal candidate will have **12-15+ years’ experience, including** **experience within a consultancy group** , as well as:

  

* Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Science/Engineering or similar with relevant experience in one or more of soils, erosion, geochemistry, risk assessment, toxicology/eco-toxicology or geomorphology. Post Grad qualifications will be held in high regard.
* Experience managing both projects, and teams of consultants across different geographies
* Proven experience in operations leadership within a technical consulting or professional services environment
* Experience in developing practice-level business plans and achieving intended outcomes, particularly for developing teams in start-up or scale up phases.
* Proven people management experience across a wide area to engage, develop and retain their team
* Demonstrated experience in consistently achieving performance metrics and growing teams, revenue and margins
* Excellent business development, client management and multi-disciplinary bid execution skills
* Outstanding ability to understand client needs and oversee teams to meet those needs
* Effective communication capabilities, particularly around conveying vision, strategic intent and ability to invigorate people to bring them on the journey
* Competence in analytical assessments and reporting

CalRecycle’s Mission: Protecting California’s environment and climate for the health and prosperity of future generations through the reduction, reuse and recycling of California resources, environmental education, disaster recovery and the transition from a disposable to a fully circular economy.

CalRecycle values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. Job Description And Duties

Do you have a passion to perform a variety of scientific, analytical, and technical assistance duties to implement enforcement requirements and assist with program analysis of compliance policies for Product Stewardship Compliance Branch? Do you enjoy working in a collaborative, dynamic environment? CalRecycle is seeking an enthusiastic Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to join our talented team that is passionate to work in the Product Stewardship Compliance programs!

Position Description:

Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager II (Supervisory) (EPM II) in the Product Stewardship Compliance Branch, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) will act as a lead technical expert on the product stewardship compliance programs. The incumbent performs difficult, complex, sensitive scientific and technical duties related to CalRecycle’s product stewardship compliance, including environmental and materials management research, analyses, investigations, and enforcement. The incumbent utilizes principles of scientific research, physical and environmental sciences, and statistical analysis, along with expertise in integrated waste management, industry economics, public health, and resource management. Responsibilities include assessing and enforcing regulations, reviewing and analyzing technical documents, evaluating operations and monitoring records, and conducting inspections and compliance assessments. The incumbent is responsible for determining the significance of violations and their general effect on public health, safety, environmental justice, and the environment for the program. Key duties include providing training and mentoring of staff in the determination of compliance with state minimum standards, offering technical expertise on evaluation and enforcement matters; reviewing findings and reports for technical adequacy; and ensuring that enforcement information in the Department’s databases has been accurately input by staff. The incumbent will independently identify problems, develop courses of action, and conduct investigations and studies that yield information and recommendations to improve the department’s oversight of product stewardship compliance programs. Additionally, the incumbent will play a key role in the development and implementation of new enforcement programs related to products with extended producer responsibility (EPR) and product stewardship requirements.

The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has an open position which will implement a monitoring program for vegetation management projects approved under the Governor’s March 1, 2025 State of Emergency.
  
  
We want you to join our small team within the Habitat Conservation Planning Branch (Branch) located in West Sacramento. Our team works on timber harvesting and fire resiliency policy for CDFW and supports a larger, statewide program of dedicated scientists.

• Coordinate with Program staff to respond to California Board of Forestry and Fire Protection proposals

• Assist with implementation of the Governor’s California Wildfire & Forest Resilience Action Plan

Project Team Management: Lead a small project team; communicate the necessary outcomes and the direction required to achieve them; coordinate team actions on project tasks; request additional team member support when needed; and identify areas of improvement to build the capability of the team through training, coaching, and mentoring.
Requirements Management: Coordinate the identification and elicitation of requirements; conduct analysis of those requirements for completion and alignment; document and manage requirements throughout the life of the project; and coordinate the verification of the end deliverable. Generally done at the level of project phases.
Willingness to respond to call outs during non-routine working hours
Act as the first point of contact for clients for new emergency projects, with ability to delegate tasks and request support as required from GHD FIRST team.

Experienced in emergency preparedness, air monitoring, environmental assessment/sampling, ICS, SCAT, PHMSA

jobs.description:
Job Overview

The APTIM Federal Services, LLC team is seeking a Field Chemist to support an existing project team at our Hunters Point Naval Shipyard Project in San Francisco, California along with other projects in and out of the Bay area as well as California in general. This position will support a variety of Field and Office/Remote Chemistry-related tasks on all phases of project activities. Environmental Laboratory experience is desired, but not a requirement.

Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities

Planning and oversight and/or completion of on-site sample collection and packaging and shipping of samples
Coordinating with subcontract laboratories
Interpretation/evaluation and verification/validation of chemical data
Assist in the development of plans, including selection of sampling and analyses methods
Data tracking and evaluations against project criteria
Preparation of procedures and reports related to sample/data collection and results
Communication of data and comparison to decision-limits to project teams, including client and/or regulator entities, ensuring conformance to applicable technical standards as well as company policies and procedures
Participation in project planning and execution should results indicate additional action is required

Basic Qualifications

Ability to work individually as well as cooperatively and be an important member of a remediation field team
Ability to prioritize assignments and work independently with minimal guidance
May act as a resource for colleagues with less experience
Monitor and control costs within own work. Solve moderately complex problems; take a new perspective on existing solutions
Manage own time to meet agreed targets
Ability to work outside in all weather conditions and on sites where hazards are present and PPE is required
Able to lift up to 40lbs
Possess ability to explain difficult issues, develop and plan solutions, and work to establish consensus
Promote teamwork; coaches and guides others.
Possess a BS Degree in Chemistry or other Environmental/Physical Science discipline
Looking for 1-3 years relevant experience, with experience in environmental investigation/remediation sampling and analysis a plus.

A leading professional solutions firm, we specialize in environmental, sustainability, resilience, and infrastructure solutions. Together, we create sustainable and resilient communities for all.

Dogged determination to deliver for our clients and communities

Investment into your personal and professional development
